articles.headline: Tyreek Hill's wife recounts assault, verbal abuse at trial
articles.description: Tyreek Hill's wife recounted details of assault and verbal abuse during testimony Tuesday on the first day of a civil assault and battery trial in Florida, proceedings that began a day after ESPN reported Hill would potentially sign an NFL contract soon.
articles.headlineJa: タイリーク・ヒルの妻、裁判で暴行と暴言について証言
articles.descriptionJa: フロリダ州で行われている民事暴行事件の公判初日となる火曜日、タイリーク・ヒルの妻は証言の中で、暴行と暴言の詳細を語った。この公判は、ヒルがまもなくNFLと契約を結ぶ可能性があるとESPNが報じた翌日に開始された。
articles.body:
NFL All-Pro receiver Tyreek Hill's wife recounted details of assault and verbal abuse during testimony Tuesday on the first day of a civil assault-and-battery trial in Florida. Some assaults occurred while she was pregnant with his daughter, Lakeeta Vaccaro testified.

Her testimony, as part of the couple's divorce proceedings, came a day after Hill's agent told ESPN's Adam Schefter that his client would potentially be signing a contract with a new team soon. NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy told ESPN on Tuesday that Vaccaro's allegations against Hill remain "under review of the personal conduct policy."

Vaccaro's allegations followed a previous case in 2014 in which another woman accused Hill of domestic violence. Hill pleaded guilty and completed three years of court-ordered probation.

Vaccaro, the sister of former NFL receiver Kenny Vaccaro, broke into tears on two occasions during more than three hours of testimony and cross-examination. Trial coverage by Law&Crime Trials appeared online via YouTube.

The abuse started on Jan. 10, 2024, she said, when she and Hill began arguing over a post-nuptial agreement he pressured her to sign. She did not sign, saying she didn't agree with certain stipulations.

Vaccaro said that "probably the worst of all these times" was a July 12, 2024, visit to Bristol, Connecticut, and ESPN headquarters. She alleged Hill attacked her while she was pregnant, attempting to punch her in the stomach following an argument. Becoming emotional for one of the only times during her testimony, Vaccaro testified she deflected the punch with her hands. "If I didn't block it," Vaccaro said, "it would just hit me."

She also alleged Hill pulled her hair, broke her sunglasses and cursed at her at a Bristol hotel.

Video taken by ESPN of the visit shows Vaccaro standing off to the side when her husband was being interviewed and smiling only briefly while standing next to Hill posing for a group photo. They did not appear to touch during the photo and appeared to walk in opposite directions after it.

The Jan. 10 argument about the post-nuptial agreement angered Hill, Vaccaro testified, and he threatened divorce, tried to take her wedding ring from her finger, grabbed a necklace off Vaccaro's neck, put his hands around her neck, grabbed and twisted her breasts and wrestled her to the bed. She took a photo of markings on her chest and said the incident "terrified" her. Vaccaro texted her mother the next day, describing aspects of the fight. The texts were entered among multiple exhibits to help corroborate her account.

In cross-examination, Hill's attorneys asked her why she hadn't taken more photos. Vaccaro said she only took the picture because the wound "was right in my face."

articles.headline: Sources: EuroLeague teams reject offer to merge into NBA Europe
articles.description: Members of the EuroLeague rejected a formal offer from the NBA this week to merge and create a single NBA Europe operation, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ユーロリーグのチームがNBAヨーロッパへの統合案を拒否
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが得た情報によると、ユーロリーグの加盟チームは今週、統合して単一の「NBAヨーロッパ」体制を構築するというNBAからの正式な提案を拒否した。
articles.body:
Members of the EuroLeague rejected a formal offer from the NBA this week to merge and create a single NBA Europe operation, sources confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday. 

The decision was made after a rare meeting among the clubs on Lake Como in Italy after the NBA had submitted the offer following more than two years working on creating the new league.

The decision by the EuroLeague clubs, who are considering their own plan to expand in the face of the NBA's planned entrance to the marketplace, was not unexpected.

The plans for NBA Europe will go forward, despite the rejection of the merger offer, with the intent of forming a 16-team league that could start as early as the 2027-28 season, sources told ESPN. The NBA has received lucrative bids on expansion franchises in cities across Europe and plans to create teams that could directly compete for fans, media rights and sponsorship dollars with the EuroLeague.

 

Another split in European basketball occurred in 2000-01, when a new league known as the ULEB broke away from the established FIBA-led league and the two had an uncomfortable, and unprofitable, divided season. The next year, the leagues combined so that both could survive and the modern EuroLeague was born.

NBA owners, who were briefed on the progress of NBA Europe during last month's board of governors meeting in New York, are behind the new venture and are looking at it as a long-term play to create value.

"This is a 20-year project," one owner told ESPN. "And that's how we're approaching it."

According to high-ranking European basketball officials who have been involved in the negotiations, a significant number of the 13 permanent EuroLeague teams have expressed an interest in joining NBA Europe. It has led to a fractured situation with many different angles and teams looking to secure their present and future. For now, though, the coalition is holding against the NBA's recruitment attempts. But negotiations are expected to continue, sources said.

The model the NBA has been interested in creating would allow teams to compete in their national leagues on desired weekend days and play in NBA Europe during the week, sources said. There would also be expanded rosters so teams can have the depth to play in multiple competitions with a focus on investing in European player development.

But the NBA's proposal, which several European media outlets have described as a "buyout" offer for the EuroLeague, so far has been rejected.

Front Office Sports first reported EuroLeague's rejection of the NBA's proposal.

articles.headline: Giants' Berrios says he'll undergo season-ending foot surgery
articles.description: Giants receiver Braxton Berrios will undergo season-ending surgery on his foot, he announced Tuesday on Instagram.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのベリオス、足の手術のため今季絶望へ
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのレシーバー、ブラクストン・ベリオスが火曜日にInstagramを通じて、足の手術を受けるため今シーズンは離脱することを発表した。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants wide receiver Braxton Berrios will need surgery on his injured foot and will miss the remainder of the season, he announced Tuesday on Instagram.

Berrios revealed the news on his 31st birthday and said, "I'd be lying if I said I wasn't miserable right now." This is his third consecutive season that has ended early because of injury.

Berrios was the Giants' primary kickoff and punt returner, in addition to being the fourth wide receiver. He had yet to catch a pass in 23 offensive snaps and was averaging 2.5 yards per punt return.

Charlie Jones, who along with Berrios was signed to the active roster last week, will step into the return role. Jones had two punt returns for 29 yards and averaged 23 yards per kickoff return on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals after Berrios was injured returning a punt late in the first half.

Coach John Harbaugh said on Monday that the Giants planned to replace Berrios primarily from within. The Giants have wide receivers Dalen Cambre and Jalin Hyatt on the practice squad. They also are signing former Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Dontae Fleming to the practice squad, per source.

"I think our first look would be internally, yes," Harbaugh said. "We've got guys that have been here practicing who are in the system, know what they're doing or are preparing for this opportunity. Kind of like we did with [outside linebacker] Trace [Ford], too. So, that would be our first look. I'm sure we'll turn over every stone, too. But sometimes the best stones are right under your feet. So, that would probably be our move, I would think."

The Giants recently released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to make room on the active roster for Berrios and Jones. It seems unlikely that Beckham would return.

Berrios is in his eighth professional season with the New York Jets, Miami Dolphins, Houston Texans and Giants. He has 140 career catches for 1,360 yards and six touchdowns as a receiver.

Berrios also has a kickoff return for a touchdown on his resume.

articles.headline: MVP?! 3 keys to watch if Panthers QB Bryce Young is on that path
articles.description: The 2023 first-round pick's start -- he leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards -- puts him in the MVP conversation.
articles.headlineJa: MVP！？パンサーズのQBブライス・ヤングがその道を突き進んでいるとしたら、注目の3つのポイント
articles.descriptionJa: 1,268ヤードのパス獲得数でNFLをリードする、2023年ドラフト1巡目指名選手の好調な滑り出しが、彼をMVP候補の一人に押し上げている。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- It was hard to ignore.

As the Bank of America Stadium crowd basked in its first home win of the 2026 season, multiple "MVP" chants erupted during the Panthers' 32-26 win against the Detroit Lions on Sunday night. The three-lettered chorus was aimed at quarterback Bryce Young as he put together an epic aerial performance.

And while it might be a bit premature for MVP consideration, especially for a signal-caller who has experienced highs and lows throughout his four-year career, Young's start to the season has undoubtedly made the conversation at least plausible as the Panthers enter their Week 5 bye and await the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6.

Young, 25, leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards. He's tied for third in passing touchdowns -- with the likes of Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes, Detroit's Jared Goff and New Orleans' Tyler Shough -- with nine.

"That's stats," Young said Sunday. "For us, the only stat we care about is the win column."

It's worth noting the Panthers (2-2) have a .500 record through the first quarter of the season for the first time since 2021, and Carolina is also 10-8 with Young as a starter dating back to Week 3 of last season. Coming off their first playoff appearance since 2017 and first division title since 2015, the Panthers currently sit at the top of the NFC South division, ahead of the Falcons (2-2).

Young is a large reason for Carolina's early success, as the Panthers have the top passing offense in the league entering Week 5. Carolina is averaging 301.3 passing yards per game, pushing the offense to rank fourth in the league with an average of 405.8 total yards per game.

And while Young says he doesn't want to focus on stats (or a potential contract extension), the weight of those aforementioned MVP chants are ultimately going to be impacted by numbers beyond the Panthers' win total.

Let's look at three stats to monitor and ones that could further influence Young's path toward the league's top award:

Bryce Young's touchdown-to-interception ratio

Young is protecting the ball quite well. Through four games, he has two interceptions and no fumbles lost. He's averaging 4.5 touchdowns for every one interception so far this season.

Of the six QBs with nine or more passing touchdowns, only Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers (1) and Goff (0) have fewer than two interceptions entering Week 5.

In his three previous seasons, Young has done a relatively good job of avoiding interceptions with the occasional multiple-pick downturn outing peppered into his annual performance. His career high for interceptions in a season is 11, which he produced while also throwing for a career-high 3,011 yards and 23 touchdowns in 2025.

articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 6: Jalen Hurts' job gets a lot tougher with Lane Johnson retirement

By Michael F. Florio

Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL on Tuesday. That will leave a massive hole on the offensive line for an Eagles team that is missing a ton of star players. Saquon Barkley hurt his hamstring and is expected to miss Week 5, DeVonta Smith missed last week due to a hamstring injury and seems unlikely for Week 5, and Dallas Goedert remains sidelined with a knee injury.

Jalen Hurts has struggled in games without Johnson, averaging 174 passing yards and 1.1 passing touchdowns per game when Johnson sat. On top of that, he faces a Jacksonville Jaguars team that has allowed three passing touchdowns to six interceptions this season. The Jaguars can get after the QB as well, producing 10 sacks through four weeks, the eighth-most in the NFL. That's problematic without Johnson.

Perhaps Hurts' rushing ability saves the day, but he has not ran as much this season. He has less than 20 rushing yards in two of his last three games and one rushing touchdown this season. Plus, the Jaguars have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and just two rushing touchdowns so far in 2026.

Some QBs I would play over Hurts are Matthew Stafford, Jacoby Brissett, Kyler Murray and Jordan Love. The "floors" are not safe, but Jameis Winston and Aaron Rodgers are upside options this week in favorable matchups.

Falcons' offense has come alive under Michael Penix Jr.

By Michael F. Florio

The Atlanta Falcons are hitting their stride with Michael Penix Jr. They scored 45 points Monday night against the New Orleans Saints and have 80 total in Penix's two starts. Penix threw for 223 yards and one touchdown, finishing with 12.72 fantasy points. He has yet to crack 15 and is primarily a superflex option, although all the QB injuries could change that.

Penix's impact on the Falcons offense cannot be overstated. Bijan Robinson went for 147 total yards and two touchdowns Monday, and in 16 career games with Penix at the helm he has 2,181 scrimmage yards and 17 touchdowns. Robinson saves his best for primetime, which means fantasy managers are in luck, as the Falcons play the Baltimore Ravens on "Sunday Night Football" next week.

Penix also continues to elevate Drake London. After going for 194 yards in Week 3, London was held to a modest 96 yards on five catches Monday. He has 105 catches, 1,576 yards and nine touchdowns in 16 career games with Penix. He has to be viewed as an elite fantasy option as long as Penix is healthy.

articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール安定度評価：2024年〜2026年
articles.descriptionJa: この安定度評価では、2024年から2026年にかけて、選手がいかに安定しており、またいかに先発起用に見合う活躍をしたかを測定しています。
articles.body:
Updated Oct. 6, 2026 (through Week 4 of 2026)

How consistency ratings work

Using fantasy points determined by ESPN's standard scoring, the charts contained in this column rate players based upon how consistently reliable they have been during the 2024 through 2026 seasons, a span of 40 weeks' worth of games (18 weeks apiece in 2024 and 2025, four so far in 2026). For IDPs (individual defensive players), the scoring from our weekly rankings is used: solo tackle (1.5), assisted tackle (0.75), tackle for loss (2), sack (4), interception (5), forced fumble (4), fumble recovery (4), touchdown (6), safety (2), pass defended (1.5). To familiarize you with the terminology and column headers listed in the charts below:

Start%: The player's "start percentage," which shows how often he earned a start in an ESPN standard PPR (points per reception) league. This is his number of "starts" -- those defined below -- divided by his number of scheduled team games.

CR: The player's "consistency rating," which is calculated as his weekly standard deviation divided by his PPR fantasy points per game average. This is meant to identify the players who were most consistently close to their weekly averages. The lower the number, the more consistent the player. Again, lower numbers are better.

nPPR%: The player's start percentage using non-PPR scoring, using ESPN's standard scoring settings without any points per reception.

FPTS/G: The player's average PPR fantasy points scored per game.

Start: The number of times that the player's point total in a given week was worthy of having had him active in an ESPN standard PPR league.

Star: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the best at his position.

Stiff: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the worst at his position, making almost any waiver-wire option a smarter choice.

These are the benchmarks for what constitutes a "start," "star" or "stiff" performance:

Sat: The number of times the player sat out a game. Players are not charged "stiff" points for sitting out, nor does it impact their overall consistency rating (CR), but it hurts their overall start percentage.

Players must have a start rate of at least 20% in either standard PPR or non-PPR scoring, rank among the top 20 quarterbacks, tight ends or kickers, top 50 running backs or wide receivers, or top 40 defensive linemen, linebackers or defensive backs, in terms of total fantasy points at their position from 2024 to 2026, or are averaging at least 50 snaps per game, for inclusion in the chart. All defense/special teams are included regardless of whether they meet those minimums.

articles.headline: Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal national team's camp after being benched. It is far from the first high-profile row of his two decades at the top.
articles.headlineJa: ポルトガル、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、レアル・マドリード：クリスティアーノ・ロナウドと監督たちの長く続く不仲の歴史
articles.descriptionJa: クリスティアーノ・ロナウドはベンチ外となった後、ポルトガル代表キャンプを離脱した。トップレベルで活躍した20年間において、こうした世間の注目を集める衝突は決して初めてのことではない。
articles.body:
Editor's note: This has been updated after Cristiano Ronaldo released a statement on the events that led to his departure from Portugal's team camp.

Was it always going to end like this? Cristiano Ronaldo -- Portugal's greatest-ever player, who led them to victory at the 2016 UEFA European Championship, and won the UEFA Champions League and the Ballon d'Or five times in a glittering club career -- walked away from the national team's camp on Wednesday, leaving his international future in doubt.

Ronaldo, 41, has since then spoken about the reasons for his departure. Days earlier, coach Jorge Jesus had insisted there was "no issue," but admitted mistakes in his handling of Ronaldo's role in Sunday's 2-1 win over Norway in the UEFA Nations League, where he was an unused substitute.

It is still unclear whether his departure means he has played his last game for Portugal. However, sources tell ESPN that Ronaldo has issued an ultimatum that he will not return to the national team while Jesus is the coach. But an acrimonious end to his international career -- during which he has scored a men's record 146 goals -- could hardly be described as a shock.

- Ronaldo goal tracker: 978 and counting on road to 1,000 career goals

- A kit fit for the GOAT: Messi's special kit for final Argentina match

- LaLiga unveils Clásico match ball for Barça vs. Real Madrid clashes

Managing the transition when an aging superstar's performance level drops is never easy, and Ronaldo's role and impact -- positive and negative -- with Portugal has been debated for three successive major tournaments now, in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

Throughout his 25-year career, Ronaldo has been involved in a series of headline-grabbing disagreements with managers, teammates and executives. As we wait for this latest drama to be resolved, here are some of the most high-profile previous examples.

Unhappy Ronaldo backs Blatter's insensitive "slavery" comparison (July 10, 2008)

Ronaldo's bid to leave Manchester United for Real Madrid that summer reached a new, histrionic high -- or low -- when Ronaldo echoed comments from then-FIFA president Sepp Blatter that keeping a player at a club against their will was comparable to "modern slavery." Ronaldo told Portugal's TV1: "It's true. I agree with what the president of FIFA said. I know what I want and what I would like. We have to see what happens. I do not know where I will begin next season." After five successful years at Old Trafford, Ronaldo was ready to move on, but United stood firm and the forward had to wait another season before his desired move to the Bernabéu was finally fulfilled.

articles.headline: Viktor Gyökeres to make Arsenal return after goal-laden stint with Sweden
articles.description: Viktor Gyökeres will return to Arsenal in confident mood after setting a new Nations League record with four more goals for Sweden over the international break.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィクトル・ギョケレス、スウェーデン代表でのゴール量産を経てアーセナルに復帰へ
articles.descriptionJa: 代表ウィーク中にスウェーデン代表としてさらに4ゴールを決め、ネーションズリーグの新たな記録を樹立したヴィクトル・ギョケレスは、自信に満ちた状態でアーセナルへ復帰します。
articles.body:
Viktor Gyökeres will return to Arsenal in confident mood after setting a new Nations League record with four goals in four games for Sweden over the international break.

Gyökeres was on target to give Sweden a 1-0 win over Romania in Bucharest on Monday night, extending his scoring streak in the competition to seven straight games.

The 28-year-old, who signed for Arsenal from Sporting Lisbon in a £64 million ($85m) deal last summer, has been used sparingly so far this season by Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, making just two substitute appearances in the Premier League.

Gyökeres, though, showed few signs of a drop in confidence over the extended international window with goals in each of the fixtures, which started with a wins over Romania and Poland in Stockholm before a 1-1 draw away to Bosnia and Herzegovina as Sweden went top of Group B4.

With Germany forward Kai Havertz picking up a hamstring issue early in the break and returning to Arsenal for further assessment, Gyokeres could be brought back in to lead the Gunners' attack when Premier League action resumes against Leeds on Saturday.

"That [the goals for Sweden] means we win three games and draw one. It is a good start to the Nations League this year and for me it feels very good," Gyökeres told reporters, as quoted by SVT Sport.

"They [Romania] had the ball a bit too much and we made it difficult for ourselves at times, but we won the match and keep a clean sheet, so after the match it is a nice feeling."

Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori got his first goal for Italy in their 3-1 win over Turkey in Bologna.

Calafiori, who scored for Arsenal after only 24 seconds in the Community Shield win over Manchester City, is hoping to continue to make plenty of contributions in the opposition box.

"Last year, I was unlucky and I was close to at least five or six goals. This year the season started quite well, but obviously, beyond the numbers, I am interested in the contribution I give to the team," Calafiori said in an interview with Rai Sport.

"I try to be well physically -- in the end that is what matters, because when I am okay I can help in so many ways."

Versatile full-back Calafiori revealed Arteta has encouraged him to make the most of his attacking instincts.

"I spoke to the coach and he himself told me that if I have this impulse to go and attack the spaces I have to do it, because it comes naturally to me," he said.

articles.headline: Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season
articles.description: It's only October, but Real Madrid already face a potentially season-defining run of five games that ends with El Clásico. What does José Mourinho need to get right?
articles.headlineJa: ムリーニョ、レアル・マドリードのシーズンを救うための課題は山積み
articles.descriptionJa: まだ10月に過ぎないが、レアル・マドリードはシーズンの運命を左右しかねない5試合の連続戦に直面している。その最後にはエル・クラシコが控えている。ジョゼ・ムリーニョに求められる正解とは何か？
articles.body:
At least Kylian Mbappé is laughing.

LaLiga is back this week, and the prognosis is already looking bleak for Real Madrid. After seven games, they trail leaders Barcelona by six points, with a high-stakes Clásico to come at Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barça's record so far is played seven, won seven. They've got a +24 goal difference, they've got Lamine Yamal, and they've got Raphinha in career-best form. From a Madrid point of view, this could get ugly.

- Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list

- Portugal, Man Utd, Madrid:  Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

But Mbappé looked carefree enough on Sunday as he posted a self-recorded video on social media, smiling while riding a bike in what looked like an idyllic country setting.

There was just one problem: his manager José Mourinho had mentioned cycling in an interview 10 days earlier, citing it as a specific example of the kind of hobbies footballers must not undertake, given their responsibilities.

"You cannot ride a bike," Mourinho said, categorically. "You fall off, and maybe you don't play three matches, or maybe worse, you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player."

Was Mbappé unaware of Mourinho's comments? Was this just an unfortunate coincidence? Or was there some other, as-yet unknown intent behind Mbappé's post, a message being sent? We'll hear Mourinho's response on Friday, as he speaks to the media the day before Madrid's game with Villarreal at the Bernabéu (stream LIVE 10/10 at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

In the meantime, Mbappé's off-field activities might not even rank among Mourinho's biggest worries this week as he works with his players on the training pitches at Valdebebas.

Mourinho has only been back at Madrid for three months. Now he has a run of five games -- Villarreal (home) on Saturday, AS Roma (away) on Oct. 14, Sevilla (home) on Oct. 18, RB Leipzig (home) on Oct. 21 and then Barcelona (away) four days later -- to get Madrid's season back on track, or risk derailing his project entirely.

So, what's the Real Madrid's to-do list ahead such a potentially season-defining set of fixtures?

Find Vinícius Júnior's best form

In eight Real Madrid games this season, Vinícius Júnior has scored just one goal, a close-range tap-in against Real Sociedad on Aug. 26. And when you look at the numbers, it gets even worse.

Take his personal, expected goal tallies against Espanyol (0.04 in 90 minutes), Málaga (0.04 in 90 minutes), Inter Milan (0.1 in 87 minutes), Rayo Vallecano (0.15 in 89 minutes) and Atlético Madrid (0.06 in 54 minutes).

Vinícius hasn't been scoring goals; he hasn't even looked like scoring goals. He's struggled to get into dangerous positions, and he's failed to convert on the rare occasions that he has.

articles.headline: Liverpool sweating over Jeremy Jacquet fitness ahead of Man City clash
articles.description: Liverpool are waiting to discover the extent of Jeremy Jacquet's fitness issue after the centre-back was left out of France's Nations League win over Belgium.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ戦を前に、リヴァプールはジェレミー・ジャケのコンディションを懸念
articles.descriptionJa: フランスのネーションズリーグにおけるベルギー戦にこのセンターバックが選出されなかったことを受け、リヴァプールはジェレミー・ジャケのコンディション不良がどの程度深刻なのかを見極めようとしている。
articles.body:
Liverpool are waiting to discover the extent of Jeremy Jacquet's fitness issue after the centre-back was left out of France's Nations League win over Belgium.

The defender had played the previous two matches, his first for the senior team, but was omitted from Zinedine Zidane's squad for Monday's 4-1 victory.

A statement from the French Football Federation said the 21-year-old had sustained a "strain to his left hamstring," while in his post-match press conference Zidane said Jacquet was "slightly injured."

Jacquet has featured in all seven matches for Liverpool this season, starting six alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence.

Head coach Andoni Iraola has cover in the form of on-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araújo and Joe Gomez, but Jacquet's potential absence for Sunday's visit of Manchester City would be a significant blow.

The Reds already have doubts over forwards Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, whose international exploits with Sweden and the Netherlands respectively were cut short.

Isak was sent home after just one match due to a minor thigh problem, with Gakpo more of a concern after injuring his ankle.

Their absence would leave Iraola short of options up front ahead of the high-profile visit of City, playing their first match since an independent commission found the club guilty of the vast majority of charges relating to financial breaches.

Summer signing Bradley Barcola could be pressed into action in a central role, even though he is more comfortable out wide, while Florian Wirtz could be moved further forward from his number 10 position.
